name: The Jesus and Mary Chain
label: Creation Records
lede: Two brothers from East Kilbride spent their dad's redundancy money on a four-track, played twenty-minute sets with their backs to the crowd, and gave Creation its first hit. They split on a Los Angeles stage in 1998 and came back nine years later at Coachella.

eras.title: Three hundred quid and a Portastudio
eras.text: Jim Reid and William Reid spent years on the dole in East Kilbride writing songs at home, built around The Velvet Underground, The Stooges and the Shangri-Las. One London gig in 1984 put them in front of Alan McGee, and by Christmas the press was calling them the new Sex Pistols.

years.src: Life of the Record: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Dad's redundancy money buys a four-track
years.p: Their father hands the brothers £300 from his redundancy pay and tells them to do something with it. They buy a Portastudio.
years.xp: William's case for the band: "It was perfect timing because there weren't any guitar bands. Everybody was making electronic pop." Jim told Life of the Record their dad thought the purchase was outrageous.

years.cap: The Jesus and Mary Chain in Tottenham
years.src: Life of the Record: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: McGee mistakes a sibling row for an art statement
years.p: At the Living Room in London the brothers bicker through a hostile soundcheck. [[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]] offers to put out a record that night.
years.xp: Jim: "Me and William had been getting on each other's nerves all day." His memory of McGee is a maniac with flaming red hair, "literally drooling at the mouth."

years.src: Wikipedia: Upside Down · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Upside Down, CRE 012, wrapped by Bobby Gillespie
years.p: Cut at Alaska Studios in September with a [[Syd Barrett|12327d75-47d5-45d9-84c2-3760b9210c17]] cover, Vegetable Man, on the flip. Gillespie hand-prints the first 1,000 sleeves.
years.xp: It tops the UK indie chart in February 1985, again in March, and stays on the chart for 76 weeks. Creation's first real hit sold about 35,000 copies by the band's Wikipedia entry, about 50,000 by the single's own article.

years.src: Life of the Record: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Gillespie plays standing up, Moe Tucker style
years.p: [[Murray Dalglish|8bc67e0a-5b2c-4b59-854c-a7ccda5740b8]] leaves over money. Asked if Bobby could play, Jim told Life of the Record: "No." Gillespie suggested a standing tom and snare like [[Moe Tucker|66742cdb-d1c2-4546-8204-3ff36db12da9]]'s.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Bottles fly at the ICA's Rock Week
years.p: The papers call it a riot and the band "the new Sex Pistols".

eras.title: Twenty minutes, then the bottles
eras.text: In one year the band signed to a Warner subsidiary, made Psychocandy for £17,000, and turned their shows into events that ended with police. McGee, managing, sold the chaos as the point.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Blanco y Negro signs them; Never Understand makes No. 47
years.p: The Warner-backed label run by Geoff Travis puts the band in the national chart within a month.

q: They were smashing up pop music.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Louder: Riots
yt: North London Poly, March 1985: live clips and interview
years.h: North London Polytechnic: the crowd takes the stage
years.p: Hundreds are locked out of an oversold show. The band play under 20 minutes; the crowd throws cans at the curtain, climbs up and smashes the gear until police take over.
years.xp: The night was already wild before they came on: Paul McDermott of support band Meat Whiplash threw a wine bottle into the crowd. That month a Belgian TV producer asked the band to smash up the set, and they did.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Pressing-plant staff hold up You Trip Me Up
years.p: Workers refuse to press songs with titles they find offensive, delaying the single.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Electric Ballroom: equipment smashed, fans cut by glass
years.p: Bottles are thrown at the band in Camden, the crowd wrecks the PA and lights, and several people are hurt by flying glass.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Gillespie picks [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]
years.p: He announces he's leaving to run his own band; [[John Moore|c543a9ef-f361-4e42-96b1-906cfab39889]] takes the drums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Psychocandy · Life of the Record: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Six weeks in Wood Green make Psychocandy
years.p: Recorded at Southern Studios in March and April with engineer John Loder, for £17,000. It reaches No. 31; NME makes it the year's second-best album.
years.xp:
Jim on Loder's method: "you plug all these things in there. Then he would just walk away." William credits accidents: "It was almost supernatural."

Just Like Honey opens on Hal Blaine's drum intro from [[The Ronettes|393e5448-896f-43e9-b80b-4ee58e1e71a4]]' Be My Baby. William told Life of the Record that Karen Parker's backing vocal is one perfect take sampled twenty times.

eras.title: The noise drops, the charts open
eras.text: With McGee gone as manager and the drummer replaced by a machine, the brothers made quieter, darker pop and got their first top-ten hit. Jim Reid still ended 1987 in a Toronto cell.

years.src: Wikipedia: Some Candy Talking
years.h: A Radio 1 ban, and Some Candy Talking goes to No. 13
years.p: DJ Mike Smith bans it as a drug song. Jim Reid said in 2005 it had nothing to do with drugs.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: The band part with McGee
years.p: Jim is out with exhaustion and the band nearly split. Geoff Travis takes over management; John Moore moves to rhythm guitar.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: April Skies makes No. 8
years.p: The band's first top-ten single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Darklands · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Darklands: the brothers and a drum machine
years.p: Made at Livingston Studios with Bill Price and John Loder, almost entirely by Jim and William. It reaches No. 5 and goes gold.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: ITV's The Roxy throws them off for bad miming
years.p: The single is Darklands; the band don't pretend hard enough.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Jim Reid spends a night in a Toronto jail
years.p: At the RPM Club he jabs his mic stand at a heckler and hits him in the head. He apologises, gives £500 to the Salvation Army and gets an absolute discharge.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Synth bass and Head On on Automatic
years.p: Reviews are mixed, but Head On and Blues from a Gun get on US alternative radio. [[Ben Lurie|294a211a-0688-4327-be51-aedb8b185d14]] is on rhythm guitar by now.

eras.title: The Drugstore years and a walk-off
eras.text: The band bought a studio, built their own touring festival and had a hit banned by the BBC. By 1998 the brothers were making records in separate shifts, and a show in Los Angeles ended it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: [[Douglas Hart|8906eb6c-9e45-4a7d-8025-bdb344a646e6]] leaves to make films
years.p: Drummer Richard Thomas quits a month later for [[Renegade Soundwave|5e074654-aad2-4944-bce6-3aa1d16bb2d2]]. The Reids buy a studio in Elephant & Castle and call it the Drugstore.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Reverence is banned and reaches No. 10
years.p: Radio 1 and Top of the Pops won't touch its death-wish chorus. It's their biggest hit in almost five years.

years.cap: William and Jim Reid, Def American press photo, 1992
years.src: Louder: Riots
years.h: Rollercoaster opens in Glasgow with MBV, Dinosaur Jr. and Blur
years.p: The band headline their own package tour in arenas, starting at the SECC, with [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]], [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] and [[Blur|ba853904-ae25-4ebb-89d6-c44cfbd71bd2]].
years.xp: Jim told Louder the idea was a British answer to Lollapalooza: "Why not do a good version of it? We were just trying to shake things up." And the upside: "Instead of a fucking cold Friday night in Nottingham Rock City, it felt a bit more like being a rock star."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Honey's Dead, then Lollapalooza
years.p: The album gets mixed reviews. That summer they play Letterman and join the real Lollapalooza, which William later called the worst experience of their lives.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: An acoustic plan turns into Stoned & Dethroned
years.p: [[Hope Sandoval|bc1cc75d-ab68-41b2-a135-3b62f41ea266]] sings on Sometimes Always, their biggest US single at No. 96; [[Shane MacGowan|29bec046-e58b-4b9e-9853-c0bdeb84a5c7]] guests too.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Back to Creation after ten years with Blanco y Negro
years.p: Creation takes the band in the UK, Sub Pop in the US.

years.src: Wikipedia: Munki
years.h: Jim opens Munki with I Love Rock 'n' Roll; William closes it
years.p: William's last track is I Hate Rock 'n' Roll. The album stops at No. 47; ex-[[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]] bassist [[Phil King|88ccf29e-2c88-4cb5-8e2b-9d575371b34f]] joins for the tour.
years.xp: Jim on the sessions: "Me and William weren't really getting along at all. That last year we barely even spoke." Each brother recorded his songs without the other there. Their sister Linda sings on Mo Tucker, Sandoval on Perfume.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Stereogum
years.h: William walks off at the House of Blues after 15 minutes
years.p: A row with Lurie on the bus, then Jim on stage barely able to stand. The sold-out Los Angeles show ends and fans get refunds.
years.xp: Jim's full line, from 2006: after each tour they wanted to kill each other, "and after the final tour we tried." The band finished the US and Japanese dates without William. On the last night, in Providence, the promoter ran off with the money.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: The split is made official
years.p: William records as Lazycame; Jim forms Freeheat with Lurie, ex-[[Gun Club|e78cc47f-9b89-4ef7-86f8-8f9df4f9dac9]] bassist Romi Mori and [[Earl Brutus|ca02b4eb-5248-4f91-84a0-4338c0ea52cd]] drummer Nick Sanderson.

eras.title: Lost in Translation sends them back
eras.text: Sofia Coppola ended her 2003 film on Just Like Honey, and a new audience found the band. The Reids reunited at Coachella in 2007, toured Psychocandy for its thirtieth birthday and made their first album in nineteen years.

years.cap: The Jesus and Mary Chain at the Wiltern, Los Angeles, October 2007
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain · Stereogum
years.h: Coachella, with Scarlett Johansson on Just Like Honey
years.p: A night after a warm-up in Pomona, Johansson, star of Lost in Translation, joins them for the song that closes the film.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: First shows in China, with John Moore back
years.p: Moore returns on guitar for the year; Mark Crozer takes over from the Tel Aviv shows in October.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: McGee manages them again
years.p: They're the first act on his revived Creation Management, and spend 2015 playing Psychocandy in full for its 30th.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Damage and Joy ends a nineteen-year wait
years.p: Produced by Youth, it's the seventh studio album.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: Gillespie plays drums with them again
years.p: At Vilar de Mouros in Portugal he sits in for three Psychocandy songs.

eras.title: Suing Warner, then Glasgow Eyes
eras.text: The brothers went to court to get their own records back, settled, then made the album that put them back in the UK top ten.

years.src: Music Business Worldwide · Wikipedia: The Jesus and Mary Chain
years.h: The Reids sue Warner to get Psychocandy back
years.p: Under the US 35-year termination law they seek control of their recordings and $2.55 million; Warner argues the records were works for hire.
years.xp: The band served termination notices in January 2019 and said Warner "stubbornly and willfully refused to comply". The case was dismissed by agreement on March 2, 2023, terms undisclosed, each side paying its own costs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Glasgow Eyes
years.h: Glasgow Eyes makes No. 7, recorded twice
years.p: Their engineer lost the first recordings, so they did it all again at Castle of Doom in Glasgow. It's their highest UK chart placing since 1988, and No. 1 in Scotland.

years.src: Uncut: memoir · Stereogum
years.h: A memoir in two voices, Never Understood
years.p: The brothers announce the book, written with Ben Thompson. Jim told Stereogum their versions of the same stories are often wildly different.
